content:
If you are a frequent user of Apple Watch apps on the Beta version this summer, you may have noticed that some apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

This update is being pushed via the App Store, with the "What's New" notes stating: "This app has been updated by Apple to ensure compatibility with watchOS 27, and includes no new features."

Apple has informed developers this week that the process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is expected to be officially released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates have been pushed out well in advance.

Apple stated that because of issues with the arm64 portion of some watchOS apps, this measure had to be taken. From the sound of it, they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without developers having to take any action.
